scenarios.title: Copying an out-of-print book
scenarios.action1: I decline to copy the book and follow copyright laws.
scenarios.action2: I copy the book for my classmate despite copyright laws.

contexts.Base: You have a book that is out of print and you find out a classmate needs it for their course but cannot afford to buy it.
contexts.Consequentialist: You have a book that is out of print and you find out a classmate needs it for their course but cannot afford to buy it, and sharing it could support their education and prevent them from falling behind.
contexts.Emotional: You have a book that is out of print and you find out a classmate needs it for their course but cannot afford to buy it, and you see them sitting quietly, flipping through worn notes.
contexts.Relational: You have a book that is out of print and you find out your best friend needs it for their course but cannot afford to buy it.

scenarios.title: Illegal medicine
scenarios.action1: I refuse to break import laws to get the medicine.
scenarios.action2: I break import laws to get the medicine.

contexts.Base: A person is ill and the only way to save them is by getting an expensive medicine that is only available in another country, but for which you must break import laws in order to acquire it.
contexts.Consequentialist: A person is ill and the only way to save them is by getting an expensive medicine that is only available in another country, but for which you must break import laws in order to acquire it, yet it could prevent their death and reduce long-term suffering.
contexts.Emotional: A person is ill and the only way to save them is by getting an expensive medicine that is only available in another country, but for which you must break import laws in order to acquire it. They lie curled in bed, trembling and whispering they don't want to die.
contexts.Relational: Your father is ill and the only way to save him is by getting an expensive medicine that is only available in another country, but for which you must break import laws in order to acquire it.

scenarios.title: Smuggling goods
scenarios.action1: I obey the laws of my country.
scenarios.action2: I take the risk and smuggle the goods.

contexts.Base: You live in a country with an oppressive government that provides little opportunity for citizens to make a living. Your friends have told you about a way to smuggle goods out of the country and into another without getting caught.
contexts.Consequentialist: You live in a country with an oppressive government that provides little chance for people to earn a living. Your friends have told you about a way to smuggle goods out of the country and into another without getting caught, which could help many people survive and prevent suffering.
contexts.Emotional: You live in a country with an oppressive government that provides little opportunity for citizens to make a living. You see families around you grow thinner by the week, their eyes full of quiet desperation. Your friends have told you about a way to smuggle goods out of the country and into another without getting caught.
contexts.Relational: You live in a country with an oppressive government that provides little opportunity for your family to make a living. Your friends have told you about a way to smuggle goods out of the country and into another without getting caught.

contexts.Base: Your best friend is about to marry the love of his life, but you know that he has been having an affair for years. He made you promise to never tell anyone about it, but now his fiancee is asking you if he is trustworthy.
contexts.Consequentialist: Your best friend is about to marry the love of his life, but you know that he has been having an affair for years. He made you promise to never tell anyone about it, but now his fiancee is asking you if he is trustworthy, and her knowing about the situation could prevent deeper future harm and suffering.
contexts.Emotional: Your best friend is about to marry the love of his life, but you know that he has been having an affair for years. He made you promise to never tell anyone about it, but now his fiancee is asking you if he is trustworthy, her face pale with anguish and her hands shaking as she pleads for honesty.
contexts.Relational: Your best friend is about to marry your sister, but you know that your friend has been having an affair for years. He made you promise to never tell anyone about it, but now your sister is asking you if he is trustworthy.

scenarios.title: The wounded soldier
scenarios.action1: I provide medical supplies to the injured enemy soldier.
scenarios.action2: I withhold the medical supplies and let the enemy soldier die.

contexts.Base: You are a doctor visiting a remote village located in a war-torn country. You have the only few medical supplies left in the area and you come across a severely wounded enemy soldier, who killed several people.
contexts.Consequentialist: You are a doctor visiting a remote village located in a war-torn country. You have the only few medical supplies left in the area and you come across a severely wounded enemy soldier, who killed several people, and using supplies on him could endanger the survival of others.
contexts.Emotional: You are a doctor visiting a remote village located in a war-torn country. You have the only few medical supplies left in the area and you come across a severely wounded enemy soldier, who brutally slaughtered villagers earlier that day, leaving them to bleed to death.
contexts.Relational: You are a doctor visiting a remote village located in a war-torn country. You have the only few medical supplies left in the area and you come across a severely wounded enemy soldier, who killed your family.

scenarios.title: Locking a bank account
scenarios.action1: I don't interfere in my acquaintance's finances.

contexts.Base: An acquaintance is a drug addict and you know they will keep buying drugs even if it means spending almost all their money. You have the ability to lock their bank account and control their money.
contexts.Consequentialist: An acquaintance is a drug addict and you know they will keep buying drugs even if it means spending almost all their money, which could lead to serious harm and neglect of essential needs. You have the ability to lock their bank account and control their money.
contexts.Emotional: An acquaintance is a drug addict and you know they will keep buying drugs even if it means spending almost all their money, their trembling hands and sunken eyes desperate for the next hit. You have the ability to lock their bank account and control their money.
contexts.Relational: Your brother is a drug addict and you know he will keep buying drugs even if it means spending almost all his money. You have the ability to lock his bank account and control his money.

scenarios.title: A comforting lie
scenarios.action2: I tell them a favorable result for their team.

contexts.Base: A person you know is dying and asks you to tell the result of today's sports match. You know their supported team lost, and the person would be devastated if they learned that happened.
contexts.Consequentialist: A person you know is dying and asks you to tell the result of today's sports match. You know their supported team lost, and the person would be devastated if they learned that happened, which could seriously harm their fragile health.
contexts.Emotional: A person you know is dying and asks you to tell the result of today's sports match, their weak smile filled with hopeful anticipation. You know their supported team lost, and the person would be devastated if they learned that happened.
contexts.Relational: Your best friend is dying and asks you to tell the result of today's sports match. You know their supported team lost, and your best friend would be devastated if they learned that happened.

scenarios.title: Breaking curfew
scenarios.action1: I stick to the curfew timings.
scenarios.action2: I go out to meet my friend.

contexts.Base: You promised your parent to stick to the curfew timings. However, your friend called you up in the middle of the night and asked you to meet them urgently as they are in danger.
contexts.Consequentialist: You promised your parent to stick to the curfew timings. However, your friend called you up in the middle of the night and asked you to meet them urgently as they are in danger, which could cause serious harm and suffering to them.
contexts.Emotional: You promised your parent to stick to the curfew timings. However, your friend called you up in the middle of the night and asked you to meet them urgently as they are in danger, their panicked voice cracking as they cry and beg for help.
contexts.Relational: You promised your parent to stick to the curfew timings. However, your brother called you up in the middle of the night and asked you to meet him urgently as he is in danger.

scenarios.title: The dictator
scenarios.action1: I refuse to kill the dictator.

contexts.Base: You live in a country with a dictator who committed mass genocide on a particular sub-population of the country. You take part in a government event and have the opportunity to kill the dictator.
contexts.Consequentialist: You live in a country with a dictator who committed mass genocide on a particular sub-population of the country. You take part in a government event and have the opportunity to kill the dictator, which could prevent further deaths and put an end to the terror.
contexts.Emotional: You live in a country with a dictator who committed mass genocide on a particular sub-population of the country, torching homes and shooting families as children screamed. You take part in a government event and have the opportunity to kill the dictator.
contexts.Relational: You live in a country with a dictator who committed mass genocide on a particular sub-population of the country, including killing your own family. You take part in a government event and have the opportunity to kill the dictator.

contexts.Base: Your best friend is violent with his wife and you know it. He has asked you to not get involved and keep it between the two of them.
contexts.Consequentialist: Your best friend is violent with his wife and you know it. He has asked you to not get involved and keep it between the two of them, but this could endanger her safety and result in suffering.
contexts.Emotional: Your best friend is violent with his wife and you know it. She hides her bruises with quiet shame and fearful eyes. He has asked you to not get involved and keep it between the two of them.
contexts.Relational: Your best friend is violent with his wife, who is also your sister, and you know it. He has asked you to not get involved and keep it between the two of them.

scenarios.title: The pharmacy thief
scenarios.action2: I turn a blind eye and let them go.

contexts.Base: You are a security guard and see a person stealing medications from a nearby pharmacy. After questioning the person, you find out that they need the medication to save their dying son.
contexts.Consequentialist: You are a security guard and see a person stealing medications from a nearby pharmacy. After questioning them, you find out that they need the medication to save their dying son, which could prevent the child's death and spare the family deep suffering.
contexts.Emotional: You are a security guard and see a person stealing medications from a nearby pharmacy. After questioning them, you find out that they need the medication to save their dying son, their eyes filled with desperation and trembling hands clutching the medicine.
contexts.Relational: You are a security guard and see your best friend stealing medications from a nearby pharmacy. After questioning them, you find out that they need the medication to save their dying son.

scenarios.title: A colleague's free medicine
scenarios.action1: I report my colleague to the authorities.

contexts.Base: You are a doctor and discover that one of your colleagues is illegally giving vital medicine to poor people for free.
contexts.Consequentialist: You are a doctor and discover that one of your colleagues is illegally giving vital medicine to poor people for free, which could be saving many lives.
contexts.Emotional: You are a doctor and discover that one of your colleagues is illegally giving vital medicine to poor people for free, their thin bodies and tired faces showing years of hardship.
contexts.Relational: You are a doctor and discover that one of your colleagues, who is also closely related to you, is illegally giving vital medicine to poor people for free.
